title: Arrays: Declaration, Initialization and Indexing
learningObjectives: Explain arrays: declaration, initialization and indexing.
Describe relevant storage, indexing and size rules.
Trace a collection operation or traversal.
Recognize bounds, lifetime or input pitfalls.
Apply the type to a practical collection task.

understand.concept: Arrays hold a fixed number of same-type elements. Indexes begin at zero; the last valid index is count minus one.
understand.whyItMatters: Fixed groups of values are useful for samples, scores, and small lookup tables.
understand.explain: Initialize arrays, verify indexes, and avoid reading or writing past bounds.

practise.guidedTask: Trace all five Arrays: Declaration, Initialization and Indexing examples. Record sizes, indexes, values and condition checks. Identify first/last valid element and relevant edge cases.
practise.independentTask: Create a small C++ data-processing program demonstrating arrays: declaration, initialization and indexing. Test typical values, empty/boundary cases, and invalid input or indexing where relevant. Explain why this collection is appropriate.
hints: Use zero-based indexes and verify bounds.
Prefer range-based traversal when index is unnecessary.
